log.q: Do team ratings, home court, back-to-backs and the injury report beat the spread?
log.rule: The model must add information the closing line has not priced: t of the model-minus-line term at least 2.
log.result: Against the close t = 1.23; the closing spread is still more accurate (10.824 vs 11.101 points). It beat ESPN's untimed opening line (59% ATS at 5+ points), mostly by knowing injury news the open predated.
log.shipped: Vault line on the Slate page, labeled context

log.q: At prices you could actually trade (Kalshi at 1pm), does the game model win?
log.rule: Moneyline YES on the side the model rates higher than its 1pm price, after fees; ladders split into halves.
log.result: Moneyline: Kalshi 1pm Brier 0.2008 beats the model 0.2057, and the edge buckets lost after fees. Spread ladder flips sign between halves. Total ladder positive in both halves but not 2 SE.

log.q: Can minutes be projected better than recent minutes, using the injury report?
log.rule: Walk-forward on 2024-25 and 2025-26 with the report 30 minutes before tip; ship if MAE beats recent minutes scaled to 240.
log.result: MAE 4.63 vs 4.75 minutes on 56,087 player-games; 5.19 vs 5.46 when a same-position teammate is out.
log.shipped: Minutes model v2 prices every prop

log.q: When a teammate sits, does a player's production per minute change, beyond his extra minutes?
log.rule: Per stat, keep the cascade only if it lowers held-out error on games with vacated usage.
log.result: MAE on games with vacated usage, without then with the cascade: pts 3.826 to 3.817, reb 1.647 to 1.646, ast 1.233 to 1.236, 3pm 0.831 to 0.841. Kept for pts, reb, fga, pra; dropped for ast, 3pm. Small effects.

log.q: Does a minutes x rate projection, blended with the price, beat Kalshi and sportsbook props?
log.rule: GO = second-half ROI > 0 with z >= 2 over 50+ games, betting the 3%+ blended edge after fees; WATCH = positive.
log.result: Only Kalshi 3-pointers (NO side) passed. Kalshi YES is overpriced in every price bucket all season. Sportsbook props: no reliable edge.

log.q: Do opponent defense, the game total, shooting volume x regressed %, form, home and rest improve it?
log.rule: Same GO rule; v2 replaces v1 if it keeps every v1 GO and lowers Kalshi log loss.
log.result: Better RMSE on every stat; Kalshi log loss better on all four (3PM 0.5285 vs market 0.5281). Kalshi points NO joins 3PM NO as GO.
log.shipped: Prop model v2 prices the board

log.q: Do per-stat memories (each volume and percentage with its own learning rate) beat one shared rate?
log.rule: Tuned on 2024-25, scored on 2025-26 with true minutes; carried into the v3 candidate if it helps.
log.result: pts MAE 3.743 to 3.721, reb MAE 1.603 to 1.591, ast MAE 1.215 to 1.213, 3pm MAE 0.816 to 0.815.

log.q: Do role, returns from absence, new-team learning and the market spread improve minutes?
log.rule: Same test set as v2 (2025-26, report 30 minutes before tip).
log.result: MAE 4.650 vs 4.690; first game back 5.04 vs 5.49. Knowing who started: 4.515.

log.q: Do full ladder distributions (minutes x production shapes) price Kalshi ladders better than v2's curve?
log.rule: Replace v2 only if every v2 GO stays GO with ROI at least v2's; then lowest Kalshi log loss.
log.result: Better probabilities (points log loss 0.5433 vs 0.5504) but the same blended edge, so the rule keeps v2.

log.q: Minutes v3 + per-stat memory together (with and without the ladder shape): replace v2?
log.result: More accurate on every stat, but Kalshi points NO slips to WATCH (YES).

log.q: Is NBA.com's starting-lineup feed accurate, and does knowing the five improve pricing?
log.rule: Same pre-registered rule; prices are 30 minutes before tip, after lineups usually post.
log.result: Right on 5,285 of 5,286 team-games; every listed inactive sat. Best accuracy yet, but backtest prices already knew the lineups.
log.shipped: Recorder logs lineup times to test the timing edge live

log.q: Move one venue's prices to another venue's line: does that consensus find mispriced Kalshi rungs?
log.rule: GO = second-half ROI > 0 with z >= 2 over 50+ games; blends fit on the first half by tip time.
log.result: Kalshi ladder leave-one-out + model: points NO and 3PM NO GO. Books to Kalshi: WATCH. Kalshi to books: no GO.
log.shipped: Consensus gap on the Edges page

log.q: Price with minutes v3 (with and without confirmed starters), everything else v2?
log.rule: Replace v2's minutes only if every v2 GO stays GO with ROI at least v2's; then lowest Kalshi log loss.
log.result: Points NO ROI 3.0% vs v2's 3.5%; with starters z 1.94, below 2.
log.shipped: v3 minutes as a logged shadow

log.q: Players who keep hitting a line ("8 of his last 10"): do they keep hitting it, and do players who beat their lines keep beating them?
log.rule: Bet OVER at 8+ of last 10 against the same line, UNDER at 2 or fewer; GO = test ROI > 0 with z >= 2 over 50+ games, and better than betting that side blind.
log.result: Sportsbooks: at 9-10 of 10 the streak said 91%, the line said 53%, it hit 50%; 8+ of 10 overs returned -7.3% (2024-25) and -15.0% (2025-26 close). Kalshi: 8+ of 10 overs -3.8%; 2-or-fewer unders +2.5%, less than betting every NO (+3.3%). At the same price a streak is worth about +3.2%: a little information, not enough to make the losing side win. Players who beat their lines one half did not the next (correlation 0.006).
log.shipped: Nothing; a myth check for the page

log.q: Can Vault tell where sharp money is, and does following it pay?
log.rule: Polymarket accounts scored walk-forward on their own trades vs the close; then copy their side later.
log.result: Sharp accounts beat the close (+0.38%, t 7 on 2,684 NFL trades; NFL-sharp accounts +1.76% on 439 NBA trades). Copying 30 min to 2 h later: -0.19%. Size alone is not skill.
log.shipped: Sharp Price page, every signal graded live

log.q: Priced at the exact ask from Polymarket's order-book archive, does copying a sharp account 15 minutes later beat the close?
log.rule: Labels from older games only; GO if the average at 15 minutes is above zero by 2+ standard errors (NFL and college, Aug 18 - Sept 29).
log.result: Copy at 15 minutes +0.09% vs the close (SE 0.59, 36 copies). The market drifts toward sharp accounts over hours (+1.05% by kickoff), not minutes; 40 trades settle nothing. Re-test declared on Oct 1-27.

log.q: Which market is sharpest on NBA game lines at tip: Polymarket, Kalshi or the sportsbooks? And does the game model add to the sharpest?
log.rule: A venue moves ahead of the sportsbook in the Slate's fallback only if its log loss is lower by 2+ SE; the model must improve the sharpest venue's log loss on games after Feb 1 by 2+ SE.
log.result: 1,300 games of 2025-26. Log loss: sportsbook 0.5751, Polymarket 0.5755, Kalshi 0.5838: Polymarket ties the sportsbook close, Kalshi trails by a hair (not significant). Model blend on later games: +0.0011 (SE 0.0011).
log.shipped: Nothing changes: the Slate keeps its fallback order, the game model stays context

log.q: Should a player on a new team (trade, signing) count toward its minutes from his first game with it?
log.rule: Minutes MAE on new-arrival team-games lower by 2+ SE, and not worse on all team-games by more than 2 SE.
log.result: New-arrival games -0.01 min (z -1.34); a mover is left out of only his first game, and teams rarely have too few players for it to matter. Where they do (7 or fewer projected, or anyone at 44+ minutes), minutes run 2 to 4 too high.
log.shipped: Roster guard: those teams and players with no minutes for their current team are priced and shown but never a call, edge, pick'em leg or shadow bet

log.q: Should the game model's season start use the new rosters (who joined and left) and reset the league scoring level?
log.rule: Each variant: first-4-weeks MAE lower by 2+ SE (margin for rosters, total for scoring level), whole season not worse by more than 2 SE.
log.result: Rosters: first 4 weeks -0.021 pts margin (z -0.69). Scoring level: first 4 weeks -0.30 pts total (z -1.89), whole season +0.10 (z 2.27); it does fix the week-1 lean (model minus close -4.2 to +0.4).
log.shipped: Neither. The Slate labels the Vault line as last season's rosters for 4 weeks, names who joined and left, and leaves out the Vault total

dont: Betting game spreads with our game model
The closing line already knows everything our model knows. Against the close the model's side won 50.8% of 2,641 games; you need 52.4% to beat the vig.
Our side won 49.9% against the closing total. The model's totals miss by more than the line does (14.852 vs 14.315 points).
At prices you could actually trade (1pm), betting where the model disagreed lost after fees at 4 of 5 edge sizes.
Sportsbook prop lines are sharp: no stat passed. The best, rebounds at a 3% edge, returned +$7.48 per $100 but could easily be luck.
No edge at any edge size on sportsbooks; Kalshi does not list them.
The mirror image of the bets that pass: YES is overpriced in every stat, so buying it loses unless our model finds a rare exception.
Accounts with a winning record do beat the closing price, but copying their side 30 minutes to 2 hours later lost money.
Size is not skill: even $100k+ tickets lost to the closing price on average.
